items.title: The use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Corporate Reporting
items.snippet: # The use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Corporate Reporting. Artifi...
items.raw_snippet: # The use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Corporate Reporting. Artificial Intelligence Technologies ("AI” or "AI technologies") such as Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Generative AI (GenAI) are developing rapidly and are being adopted across many sectors, processes and areas of business. In corporate reporting, however, the pace of adoption is more measured. To understand how corporate reporting is adapting to the use of AI technologies, the FRC commissioned Lancaster University to undertake interviews and a survey with key stakeholders in the reporting process. The resultant research, including the survey results, shows that the use of AI technologies is increasing, especially the use of GenAI, but adoption remains controlled, targeted and uneven. However, our survey shows that mature technologies outside of AI technologies are already widely used in the corporate reporting process. ## Adoption of AI technologies.

items.snippet: ## The Pentagon’s AI Strategy Has a Funding Problem. ## Cogs of War. The Pentago...
items.raw_snippet: ## The Pentagon’s AI Strategy Has a Funding Problem. ## Cogs of War. The Pentagon’s AI Strategy Has a Funding Problem. The harder challenge is execution, and a fiscal squeeze on the Fiscal Year 2026 operations and maintenance accounts threatens to stall it before it begins. But it includes no dedicated funding for the AI software that the president’s directives require. The software that those directives call for is bought with operations and maintenance dollars, and the Iran war has drained those accounts. As a provider of AI-enabled military planning software now used across multiple combatant commands, we at Onebrief do have a commercial interest in the AI software funding this piece argues for. They are building exactly what the president’s directives say the government must have, in a fiscal year that is running short on both time and money. The Pentagon created a dedicated software appropriation in recent years, but it remains a limited pilot, and most fielded command tools are still bought the way other recurring services are, with operations and maintenance dollars.

Established in 2017, the BCAI drives the deployment of cutting-edge Industrial AI technologies across Bosch, creating solutions that are “Invented for life.” Operating from various Bosch Research locations globally, including the United States, China, India, Germany, and Israel, the BCAI conducts cutting-edge research using one of the world's largest datasets.
